title: Honors Seminar: Clown Business
description: Explore finding the personal freedom and confidence to speak your mind from your authentic self. Use clown, theatre, and your imagination to engage and enchant your audience, whether of 1 or 100. Curiosity is the only prerequisite. A safe nonjudgmental space. Play with your imagination, build confidence and poise. Stretch your mind and imagination. Freedom to be who you are comes from within. Empower yourself to own your freedom by practicing seeing further than your assumptions and clearer than your fear. There is a reason people go to see theater and plays. PLAY (P – Practice, L – Laughing, A – At, Y – Yourself) is not only one of the roots of joy it can also be the foundation of creativity and discovery.
prerequisites_raw: Enrollment in Letters and Science Honors Program.

title: Pluralism in the Military
description: Militaries are premier symbols of national identity. But how do militaries engage the identities of the soldiers. This seminar will read six books on religion, ethnicity, Race, and gender in the Military. Students will have the opportunity to discuss the books with their authors.
prerequisites_raw: Enrollment in Letters and Science Honors Program.

title: Understanding Support for Gender Equality
description: What factors make some people more likely to support gender equality than others? In this course, you will work with members of the Applied Evolutionary Anthropology Lab in the Department of Anthropology to research this question. As a group, we will review the background literature and conduct a novel investigation, drawing on data from rural Tanzania and on campus. This course will be relevant for those interested in anthropology, sociology, gender studies and research design.
prerequisites_raw: Enrollment in Letters and Science Honors Program.

title: Creative Writing in Spanish
description: This seminar offers students the opportunity to explore creative writing in Spanish through poetry, short fiction, and hybrid forms. Emphasizing voice, style, and experimentation, the course encourages students to engage writing as a critical and expressive act. Readings from contemporary authors across the Spanish-speaking world will accompany generative exercises and peer workshops. All work is conducted in Spanish. Open to heritage speakers and advanced learners committed to developing their creative voice. No prior experience in creative writing required.
prerequisites_raw: Enrollment in Letters and Science Honors Program.

title: Honors Seminar: Classical Music and Opera: An Introduction to live performances
description: Discover the beauty of classical music and opera through this course which will introduce you to the intersecting worlds of Opera, Orchestra, and Chamber Music/Recital. You will attend live performances presented by various professional organizations in the Santa Barbara area. The mission of the course is to instill a deeper appreciation of the artistry that goes into the creation of each of these beautiful art forms. For full seminar description go to College of Letters & Science Honors website: https://www.duels.ucsb.edu/honors/experiences#seminars
prerequisites_raw: Enrollment in Letters and Science Honors Program.

title: Honors Seminar: Food, Science, and Cooking
description: This seminar looks at the many connections between food, science, and cooking. We will learn about the chemistry of cooking, students will prepare presentations (and share recipes), and we will have the opportunity to visit some local food production companies. For full seminar description go to College of Letters & Science Honors website: https://www.duels.ucsb.edu/honors/experiences#seminars
prerequisites_raw: Enrollment in Letters and Science Honors Program.

title: Honors Seminar: Freedom
description: Freedom is one of the most important concepts in modern political philosophy and modern political life as well as in other spheres of life, such as religion, ethics, economics, and art. Accordingly, we will read a range of texts, including selections from the Bible, theological writings, historical narrative, philosophical essays and lectures, and political theory. We will address key questions related to freedom. For full seminar description go to College of Letters & Science Honors website: https://www.duels.ucsb.edu/honors/experiences#seminars
prerequisites_raw: Enrollment in Letters and Science Honors Program.

title: Honors Seminar: So You’re New? Organizational Assimilation: Entering and Becoming a Member
description: As a newcomer to the university, this is a topic of concern to most freshmen. In this class, we will talk about organizational assimilation, the process of becoming integrated into the culture of an organization whether it is a new job, social club, or school. In this class we’ll examine what occurs as newcomers join organizations focusing on the communication between newcomers and existing members. Students also will learn why assimilation can feel so stressful and what they can do to ease their transition.
prerequisites_raw: Enrollment in Letters and Science Honors Program.
